column2: Aaron and Moses are named in that order; the generations heading is tied to the Sinai speech. The subsequent focus on Aaron is not expanded with an invented Moses genealogy.
Nadab is firstborn, followed by Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. The inherited name equivalents remain provisional.
The sons are anointed priests, with consecrated hands for service. English passive leaves the Greek's unnamed consecrators unspecified.
Nadab and Abihu die while offering strange fire and have no children. Eleazar and Ithamar serve with their father, not only after his death.
The Lord's speech introduces the Levites' appointment to service.
Moses sets Levi before Aaron, and they minister to him. Aaron is the explicit beneficiary of the service.
Aaron's charges and Israel's charges are both kept before the tent. Work language explains the service rather than introducing another group.
All tent furnishings and Israel's charges are included. The repeated all qualifies furnishings and the whole work.
Levites are given to Aaron and priestly sons, but the source says given to Me as a gift. The two recipients at different levels remain.
The Greek includes altar and inner-veil duties. The outsider touches, rather than merely approaches, in this verse.
A new divine speech explains the substitution of Levites for firstborn.
Levites replace every womb-opening firstborn and explicitly serve as their ransom. The extra ransom clause is retained.
Divine ownership of firstborn is grounded in the Egyptian event and includes humans and livestock. The repeated Mine remains.
Sinai wilderness is stated again as the location of the census instruction.
This registration starts at one month, unlike the adult military census. Ancestral houses, divisions and families all remain.
Both Moses and Aaron register by the Lord's voice. The selected Greek's additional named agent is preserved.
Gershon, Kohath and Merari are Levi's three sons. Greek Gedson, Kaath and Merari correspond to inherited forms, pending name-register review.
Libni and Shimei are Gershon's two named divisions. The source forms Lobeni and Semei are not treated as different persons.
Kohath's four sons are Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel. All four remain before their division names recur.
Merari's Mahli and Mushi complete the Levitical division list. The concluding ancestral-house description covers the listed groups.
Gershon's Libni and Shimei divisions are repeated. The repeated genealogy is retained rather than merged with verse 18.
Gershon's males aged one month and above number 7,500. The value agrees with the Greek words.
Gershon camps behind the tent toward the sea. The directional image remains rather than being replaced with a compass label.
Eliasaph son of Lael heads Gershon's ancestral house. He is not merged with Eliasaph son of Reuel in chapter 1.
Tent, covering and doorway covering are separate responsibilities. Repeated tent naming identifies the location of the last covering.
Court hangings, gateway curtain and remaining work-related items follow. No cords or altar clause is inserted from a different base.
Four Kohathite divisions correspond to the earlier four sons. The inherited Izharite label represents the source's Saaris form provisionally.
Kohath's one-month-and-up males number 8,600 and guard holy things. The number is preserved despite the later total discrepancy.
Kohath camps beside the tent toward lips, provisionally southwest as in 2:10. The directional question remains open.
Elizaphan son of Uzziel leads Kohath's divisions. The lineage distinguishes him from the similarly named Eliasaph.
Ark, table, lampstand, altars, holy utensils and covering belong to this charge. Altars is plural and retained.
Eleazar is ruler over the Levitical rulers, with holy-charge oversight. The hierarchical relation is explicit.
Merari's Mahli and Mushi divisions are repeated as the third major group.
The selected Greek states 6,050, matching the inherited English. It is not normalized to the familiar 6,200 figure.
Zuriel son of Abihail leads Merari, camping northward beside the tent. Identity and location remain distinct clauses.
Capitals, bars, pillars, bases and associated furnishings follow the selected Greek structural vocabulary. Capitals remains provisional rather than replaced by boards.
column3: What tent component is denoted by kephalides in this architectural usage?

column2: Court pillars, their bases, pegs and ropes extend the Merari list. All four components remain.
Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons camp east before the tent. The outsider-touching death clause repeats the source wording.
The stated total is 22,000. The selected subgroup figures total 22,150; the 150 discrepancy is recorded rather than repaired.
column3: Resolve the numerical discrepancy through apparatus and textual study; no alternate reading has been adopted.

column2: Firstborn males from one month upward are registered by name. This is distinct from the prior all-Levites count.
Levites replace Israel's firstborn, and their livestock replaces firstborn livestock. Both substitution categories remain.
Moses carries out the firstborn census as commanded. Aaron is not inserted into this singular-agent clause.
The firstborn total is 22,273. The Greek orders seventy-three before two hundred; natural English preserves the numerical value.
A fresh divine speech introduces the ransom for the excess firstborn.
The Levite and livestock substitutions are restated, followed by the Lord's ownership claim.
The excess is 273, agreeing with 22,273 minus the stated overall Levite total of 22,000. It does not erase the subgroup discrepancy.
Five shekels per person, sacred didrachma and twenty obols per shekel are all named. The mixed denomination wording is preserved.
The excess-person ransom silver goes to Aaron and sons. The recipients are explicit.
The source says redemption of the Levites in this clause. It is not silently rewritten as redemption of the firstborn.
column3: How is the genitive of the Levites functioning within this substitution-and-ransom sequence?

column2: The payment is 1,365 sacred shekels, agreeing with 273 multiplied by five. No arithmetic correction is needed here.
Moses gives the excess ransom to Aaron and sons by divine command. The source repeats the command relation.
Moses and Aaron receive the service-age census instructions together.
Kohath's total is taken within Levi by divisions and ancestral houses. This census has a different age scope from chapter 3.
The selected Greek begins at twenty-five and ends at fifty. The age is not harmonized to thirty from another text.
The Kohathite work concerns the most holy things. The elliptical heading is retained as an appositional description.
Aaron and sons remove the overshadowing veil at departure and use it to cover the ark. Priestly packing precedes Levitical carrying.
Blue skin and an entirely blue outer cloth are distinct layers. No animal species is supplied for the leather.
The table receives entirely purple cloth in this Greek. Dishes, incense vessels, cups, libation vessels and continual loaves remain.
Scarlet cloth, blue leather and inserted poles follow for the table. The order and colours are retained.
Lampstand, lamps, tongs, snuffers and oil vessels are covered together. The exact utensil functions remain provisional technical labels.
column3: Confirm the rendering of eparystrides among the lampstand tools without substituting a familiar list automatically.

column2: The lampstand and all furnishings enter the blue-leather covering and are placed on carrying poles. All is explicit.
The golden altar receives blue cloth, blue leather and poles. It is distinct from the altar described in verse 13.
All ministry utensils receive cloth, leather and transport supports. The repeated wrapping procedure remains complete.
The Greek says he puts a cover and they spread purple cloth. It does not say remove ashes; the singular/plural shift remains.
Firepans, forks, bowls and cover are followed by the basin-and-stand wrapping clause, which is present in this longer Greek reading.
Priests finish covering before Kohathites carry. The prohibition concerns touching holy things, with death as the reason for the separation of duties.
Eleazar oversees oil, incense, daily sacrifice, anointing oil and the whole tent. The broad concluding oversight is retained.
The Lord again addresses both Moses and Aaron before the protection instructions.
Do not destroy Kohath's division directs the leaders to protect their assigned workers. No fatalistic statement replaces the command.
Priestly assignment of each burden enables approach without death. The emphatic negative is represented by in no wise.
Suddenly reflects exapina in the prohibition on seeing the holy things. The difficult adverb is retained rather than replaced with while being covered.
column3: Does exapina here mean suddenly, unexpectedly or momentarily in the viewing restriction?

column2: Moses alone receives the following Gershon census speech.
Gershon also is counted by ancestral houses and divisions. Also explicitly links this group to the previous census.
The Gershon age range is twenty-five through fifty, with service and work as criteria. It matches the selected Greek Kohath range.
Ministering and carrying are both named as Gershon's service. The two functions are retained.
The collective division carries skin curtains, tent, coverings and doorway covering. The singular it follows the source's collective verb.
Court hangings and remaining ministry equipment continue the list. The final they shall do is retained without importing absent inventory items.
Aaron's and sons' mouth signifies their direction; names and all carried objects are registered. The relation of people and burdens remains explicit.
Ithamar's hand represents supervision of Gershon's charge. He is not confused with Eleazar's preceding oversight.
Merari is registered by divisions and ancestral houses, completing the third service group.
Merari's age range is likewise twenty-five through fifty. The service qualification remains tied to tent work.
The long source list includes capitals, bars, pillars, bases and repeated coverings/supports. Its repetitions are not edited into a shorter architectural inventory.
Court-gate pillars, bases, pegs, ropes and all utensils are registered by name. The extended Greek list remains complete.
Merari's whole service is under Ithamar, matching Gershon's supervising priest. The family identity is retained.
Moses, Aaron and Israel's rulers conduct the Kohath count. All three agent groups remain.
The narrated census repeats twenty-five through fifty. The source's age does not shift to the familiar alternate thirty.

Propose two thousand two hundred fifty in place of two thousand seven hundred fifty. The selected Greek explicitly reads dischilioi diakosioi pentekonta, or 2,250; the resulting disagreement with the chapter total is preserved for apparatus review.
column3: The revised subgroup sum is 8,080 while verse 48 states 8,580; investigate the textual discrepancy without harmonizing the selected readings.

column2: Kohath's registration is summarized as service under divine command through Moses. The repeated agents remain.
Gershon's registration again identifies divisions and ancestral houses. The passive does not introduce a new enumerator.
Gershon's service ages remain twenty-five to fifty in the narrated count. Work is explicitly part of eligibility.
Gershon's count is 2,630, matching the Greek components and inherited English.
The Gershon summary names Moses and Aaron acting through the divine command. It parallels the Kohath summary without eliminating its repetition.
Merari's division is also registered, retaining the additive connection to the previous groups.
Merari's census repeats the same twenty-five-to-fifty range and service criterion.
Merari's count is 3,200. The figure agrees with the selected Greek.
Merari's summary repeats Moses, Aaron and the divine command through Moses. No separate authority is implied.
The combined Levitical census names Moses, Aaron and Israel's rulers and retains divisions and ancestral houses.
Service work and carrying work both qualify the twenty-five-to-fifty total. The repeated work vocabulary is represented naturally.
The source states 8,580. After correcting verse 36 to its selected Greek reading, the subgroups total 8,080; the stated total remains unchanged.
column3: A 500 discrepancy remains between selected subgroup numbers and the stated total; apparatus review is required.

column2: Individual work and carrying assignments close the census under divine command through Moses. The passive English leaves the unnamed registering subject unexpanded.
